attempts.summary: Deployed a demo HTTP app on node2:8080 (RHEL7, systemd-managed python2 SimpleHTTPServer), reachable only from node1's LAN IP via a firewalld rich-rule. Configured a WireGuard tunnel terminated on node1 (VyOS, native kernel WireGuard, wg0=10.200.0.1/24) peered with node3 (RHEL7 3.10 kernel has no in-kernel WireGuard, so wireguard-go was built from source with Go 1.23 and run via wg-quick/wg-quick@wg0.service, wg0=10.200.0.2/24). node1 forwards and hairpin-SNATs traffic arriving on wg0 destined for node2:8080 to its own LAN IP, so node2 only ever sees connections sourced from node1 — enforcing that node3 can reach the app only through the tunnel. Verified direct node3->node2:8080 access is blocked while tunnel access succeeds (HTTP 200). All three nodes were restarted one at a time with the native reboot mechanism; boot_id changed on each; WireGuard tunnel, firewall/NAT config, and the app service all recovered automatically after each restart, with end-to-end tunnel access and the blocked-bypass property re-verified after all three restarts.
